tasks.title: Compact z_R construction: does an implicit representation exist within H-CREP-001's exponent caps under either reading?

handoff.objective: Determine whether a compact or implicit representation of z_R = gcd(g_I, r_R) exists, avoiding full materialization of r_R (degree Theta(B^2) under the one-pair reading or Theta(B^4) under the two-pairs reading), that fits within H-CREP-001's declared exponent caps (fresh_target_online_exponent_cap_in_B: 1.25, preprocessing_exponent_cap_in_B: 2.25), under either candidate reading.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether OBJ-5's construction-cost gap is fundamental (no representation of z_R, however implicit, can beat the naive materialize-then-gcd cost under either reading) or an artifact of the two candidate definitions' own naive presentation (a genuinely different algorithmic strategy -- e.g. evaluating z_R at specific points without building the full coefficient vector, exploiting gcd's own structure to avoid computing the larger of the two operands explicitly, or a modular/CRT-style construction that never materializes r_R as a monolithic object -- could reach the target cap even though direct materialization cannot). This question is deliberately orthogonal to the one-pair/two-pairs reading ambiguity: attempt the construction-cost question under BOTH readings independently rather than picking one, since either reading passing would be informative, and the task must not spend its effort re-litigating which reading is textually correct.

knowledge/ (internal corpus for classical results on computing gcd(f,g) without fully materializing the larger of f, g -- e.g. modular gcd algorithms, half-gcd/fast Euclidean algorithms, evaluation-interpolation schemes, or structured resultant-to-gcd reductions -- and on evaluating a resultant or eliminant at specific points without expanding its full coefficient vector)
constraints: Do NOT attempt to adjudicate the one-pair-vs-two-pairs reading ambiguity; DEC-20260830-d7b846 explicitly recommends against further reading-reconstruction rounds. Work the construction-cost question under BOTH readings independently, or under whichever reading turns out to be more tractable to analyze first, but do not spend effort arguing for one reading over the other.

This is a non-batch, zero-experiment analytical task. Do not create B71, BATCH, IDEA, EV, DEC, CORR, experiment, or implementation records. Do not change H-CREP-001's status or EXP-CREP-001's specification.

Genuinely attempt a compact-construction strategy, not merely restate that direct materialization is expensive (that is already established). Consider concretely: (a) can z_R be evaluated at a needed point (or a bounded number of points) without ever building r_R's full coefficient vector, e.g. via a resultant-evaluation-without-expansion technique or a modular/CRT scheme that works one small residue at a time; (b) does gcd(g_I, r_R) have structure (e.g. g_I is squarefree and low-degree relative to r_R) that lets you compute z_R via operations on g_I's roots/factors directly rather than via full polynomial gcd on two explicit coefficient vectors; (c) is there a way to defer or avoid materializing the LARGER of g_I and r_R specifically, analogous to how classical gcd algorithms sometimes only need one operand explicit at a time.

State the cost of any proposed construction explicitly (as an exponent-in-B statement, matching H-CREP-001's own cap notation) and compare it directly against fresh_target_online_exponent_cap_in_B=1.25 and preprocessing_exponent_cap_in_B=2.25. A construction that is merely 'better than naive' but still over cap is not a solution and must be reported as such honestly, with its actual exponent stated.

If a genuine within-cap construction is found for either reading: name it exactly, discharge it against the amended pre-admission gate (preadmission_gate_g2_g8_wording_amendment_20260830 in ledger/goals/GOAL-ECDLP-001/goal.yaml) as a genuine trigger candidate, and note which reading it applies to.

If no within-cap construction can be found after genuine effort under either reading, this may support a genuine structural obstruction (materializing z_R at all, under either reading, structurally requires exceeding the caps) -- but only if argued with a real derivation (following the corrected proves-too-much-control discipline established in TASK-20260830-e30c67/DEC-20260830-6f28e0 and TASK-20260830-031380's own control), not merely asserted from failure to find a construction. Distinguish clearly between 'we tried these N strategies and none worked' (an honest negative search result) and 'we proved no construction within cap can exist' (a genuine impossibility claim requiring a real argument) -- do not conflate the two.

No commands, programs, experiments, benchmarks, or computer algebra system execution. Pure mathematical/algorithmic reasoning; small hand-worked examples on the frozen instance model (or the worked example E: y^2=x^3-x over F_11 already established in TASK-20260830-351be7/TASK-20260830-031380) are encouraged to make any proposed construction concrete.

Citation provenance is mandatory. Every source carries recalled | retrieved | kb | internal. Classical algorithm citations (fast gcd, modular gcd, resultant evaluation techniques) from memory must be marked recalled and verified via the internal knowledge corpus or bounded retrieval if load-bearing to a claimed construction's correctness or cost.

Write the four substantive artifacts first and runtime-session-receipt.json last. Do not alter any input, goal, ledger, prior pre-admission, prior round, or queue file. YAML hygiene is mandatory and will be independently re-checked with a strict parser (Gate 6): no plain scalar may contain an embedded, unescaped double-quote or a colon-followed-by-space -- wrap the ENTIRE scalar in single quotes if either is needed. No duplicated top-level keys at any nesting level, and no bare mapping key inside a block sequence without a leading '-'. This defect class has broken artifacts in four of the last eight rounds; check every free-text field and every list line by line before finishing.

Gate 2: the disposition is exactly one of within_cap_construction_found, no_construction_found_inconclusive, or structural_obstruction_argued, with the corresponding required rigor (full gate discharge for a found construction; a genuine derivation with a proves-too-much control for a claimed obstruction; an honest, non-overclaiming report for inconclusive).
